newsitem.title: USA: Oil prices to squeeze Ashland earnings.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices to squeeze Ashland earnings.

text.p: The recent run-up in crude oil prices is expected to trim Ashland Inc earnings for the fourth quarter ending September 30, said Paul Chellgren, president and chief operating officer.

The diversified independent refining and marketing company, which buys most of the crude oil processed in its U.S. refineries through contracts or on the spot market, signalled to analysts within the past two weeks its projections of lower- than-expected earnings, he said in an interview.

"This quarter we think earnings might be in the 70 cents (a share) or less range, and that was a bit less than the market assumed, say, thirty or sixty days ago, so we've had to bring analysts' estimates down for our fiscal year," he said.

Analysts currently expect Ashland to post between $0.60 and $1.04 a share earnings in the fourth quarter with a mean estimate of $0.78 a share, according to First Call. The company through nine months ended June 30 reported $2.34 a share earnings, including a $0.74 a share one-time gain.

The Ashland, Ky.-based company with the release of third- quarter earnings in July said it was optimistic about results for the fourth quarter and the year because of strength in its chemical, construction and Valvoline lubricants businesses.

But the run-up in crude prices on tensions in the Middle East dampened that outlook. "In essence the sole reason has been the rapid run-up in crude prices," said Chellgren, who becomes Ashland chief executive officer on October 1 and is slated to be named chairman in January 1997.
